opportunities.title: Fix the front door: claim the Google profile and give the site one working, agent-readable enquiry path
opportunities.problem: Both published ways of reaching the firm are broken or missing. The contact form has five fields and a Submit button but no working submit path, the phone number is plain text on an https page with telephone auto-detection disabled, the mobile hamburger opens nothing, the Google listing is unclaimed with no hours and no photos, and there is no structured data or meta description for a search engine or AI assistant to read services and service area from. A prospect who prefers web over phone simply disappears, and the firm cannot see that it happened.
evidence: Contact form posts to javascript:void(0); jQuery is loaded over plain http://code.jquery.com on an https page so it is blocked and the validate/ajax handlers never bind - submitting does nothing (confirmed by triage wrong_claims, not just a page read) - https://stoneridgeeng.com/contact.html
Phone number is not a tel: link and the viewport meta sets format-detection telephone=no, so there is no tap-to-call on a phone - https://stoneridgeeng.com/index.html

At 390px the hamburger does nothing (mmenu depends on the same blocked jQuery, menu container stays at opacity 0), so About, Services and Contact are unreachable from the mobile header - https://stoneridgeeng.com/index.html

Google Business Profile shows 'Claim this business', 'Add hours' and 'Add photos'; 5.0 rating with no review count visible - https://www.google.com/maps/search/Stone+Ridge+Engineering+North+Brunswick+NJ
No JSON-LD, no meta description, page-name-only titles ('Home | StoneRidge Engineering, LLC.'), robots.txt 404 (nothing blocked, but nothing declared either) - https://stoneridgeeng.com/index.html
Contact page's map embed carries an October 2016 timestamp and renders as a blank block occupying most of the 390px viewport above the contact heading - https://stoneridgeeng.com/contact.html
Business hours are absent from both the site and the Google profile, so after-hours expectations are undefined - https://stoneridgeeng.com/contact.html
opportunities.agent_design: Static repair plus a small claiming/response loop, not a chatbot. Work: replace the dead jQuery stack with dependency-free JS; point the form at a real endpoint with server-side validation, a confirmation screen, an autoresponder and an email/SMS notification to Cioffi; add tel: links and make the 390px nav work; add ProfessionalService/LocalBusiness JSON-LD with services, address, area served and hours; write per-page titles and meta descriptions naming MEP engineering and North Brunswick; replace the 2016 map embed. Then a review-request agent: after a project closes (trigger = invoice paid, logged manually at first), draft a short review request for Cioffi to approve and send, and watch the profile for new reviews and unanswered questions. Humans approve: all outbound review requests and any public reply to a review; Cioffi completes the Google claim and verification himself (the consultant cannot log into his account).
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is a code and listing repair, not a subscription: mixed-content and jQuery debugging, a working form endpoint with spam handling, schema markup kept in sync with services, and a Google claim that only the owner can verify. It also has to come first - there is no working intake for any other agent to sit on top of.

impact_estimate.range: Today: 0 of 1 web forms can be submitted, 0 of 1 phone numbers are tappable, 1 of 1 Google profiles is unclaimed with no hours or photos, and 0 of 6 pages carry structured data. After: 1 working form with confirmation and alert, tap-to-call on every page, a claimed profile with hours, services and photos, and 6 marked-up pages. Deliberately no dollar figure - no sourced benchmark exists for recovered enquiries at a 3-10 person engineering firm, and the site has no analytics to measure a baseline.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes enquiry volume is greater than zero but unknown: there is no analytics tag, no call tracking and no review count to establish today's traffic. The only defensible conversion is time, priced at the NJ civil engineer median of $104,660/yr ($50.32/hr) from the brief - i.e. the principal's own follow-up and re-keying time, not revenue.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: rewritten contact page and form with a live endpoint, autoresponder and notification email; working mobile nav; tel: links; JSON-LD plus titles and meta descriptions on all six pages; Google profile claimed and completed with hours, services and photos; mobile check at 390px on real hardware; a simple enquiry log (timestamp, source, status) so the firm can see what arrives.

opportunities.title: Enquiry-to-proposal agent: scope the request, draft the fee proposal, chase the follow-up
opportunities.problem: Every enquiry arrives as a phone call or a five-field free-text comment (name, address, phone, email, comments) with no questions about building type, square footage, existing systems, deadline or decision stage, so Cioffi hand-qualifies each one. Every deliverable - due diligence report, feasibility study, peer review, design package - needs scoping plus a written proposal before work starts, and with word-of-mouth intake there is no qualification or CRM step at all between the enquiry and the principal.
evidence: Only intake paths are the phone and a comments-only form; no scope questions, no quote or scheduling flow - https://stoneridgeeng.com/contact.html

Deliverables are document-heavy and each requires scoping plus a written proposal before work begins (due diligence reports, feasibility studies, peer reviews, design documents) - https://stoneridgeeng.com/due-diligence.html
Firm describes itself as built on word of mouth and repeat customers, with no visible CRM, marketing or BD contact on the site - https://stoneridgeeng.com/

O*NET 41-3091: 'Develop sales presentations or proposals to explain service specifications' importance 84 (Core); 'Quote prices, credit terms, contract terms, or fulfillment dates for services' importance 76; 'Maintain customer records using automated systems' 76 - https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/41-3091.00

O*NET 17-2051: 'Prepare or present public reports on topics such as bid proposals...' importance 63 and 'Estimate quantities and cost of materials, equipment, or labor' 64 - the estimating/proposal workload of an engineering consultancy - https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/17-2051.00

ACEC Research Institute 2025 survey: AI use is most common in marketing and sales (81% of firms) and AI-assisted proposal development is a named common application; 68% estimate AI could automate up to 29% of current tasks (self-reported expectations, not measured savings) - https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/

Only one principal engineer is named for the firm, so proposal and report writing most likely queue behind him (inference from the about page naming Cioffi and no other role) - https://stoneridgeeng.com/about.html
opportunities.agent_design: Event-driven intake agent triggered by a form submission, an inbound email, or a call note transcribed by staff. Step 1: ask the qualification set the firm currently asks by voice - service line, building type, square footage, existing MEP/FP systems, scope of work, deadline, decision stage, architect/owner/tenant role - and record answers against the enquiry. Step 2: classify the request into one of the firm's service lines and check it against a capacity and fee-band card. Step 3: draft a scoped proposal in the firm's own template (basis of design assumptions, deliverables, exclusions, fee as a range, schedule), pulling language from prior proposals for that service line. Step 4: queue follow-ups at 3, 7 and 14 days with a short, specific nudge; log every state change into a lightweight pipeline table/board. Humans approve: Cioffi reviews and sets every fee and scope, and nothing leaves without his send; the agent never issues engineering opinions, never signs or seals anything, and flags out-of-scope or high-risk requests (e.g. life-safety, emergency power) straight to him.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: It has to hold state across weeks of email, write into the firm's proposal template, keep a fee-band card and a priors corpus, and enforce an approval gate before anything reaches a client. A chatbot subscription cannot run multi-week follow-up, cannot log to a pipeline, and cannot be trusted with client scope language unrevised. Confidential bid and fee data also argues for a restricted deployment where client documents are not spread across third-party tools.

impact_estimate.range: 1-3 hours of principal time saved per enquiry-to-proposal cycle; at the NJ civil engineer median of $104,660/yr ($50.32/hr) that is roughly $50-$150 per proposal, or ~$200-$1,200/month if the firm turns 4-8 proposals in a month (volume unknown).
impact_estimate.assumptions: Applies the measured drafting speed-ups as a transfer, not a local measurement: 25.1% faster task completion and 12.2% more tasks on consulting tasks inside AI capability (BCG field experiment, Organization Science 2025) and a 40% cut in completion time on 20-30 minute professional writing tasks (Science 2023, preregistered experiment with 453 professionals). Savings are on drafting, scoping write-up and follow-up admin - not on engineering judgement, and not on fee accuracy, which stays with the principal. Proposal volume per month is an assumption: no public source states it.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-4 weeks: qualification form and intake agent live for one service line (due diligence is the best first pick), a fee-band and exclusions card built with Cioffi from 10 historical proposals, draft proposals for the first 5 real enquiries with an approval step before send, automated 3/7/14-day follow-ups, and a pipeline board plus a weekly hours-saved log so the first month produces a measured baseline.

opportunities.title: Private knowledge agent over the firm's own reports, specs and standard details, with PE review built in
opportunities.problem: The firm's product is documents, and the same questions repeat: what did we assume for this building last time, what code basis did we use, what did the peer review flag, what is our standard detail for this system. With one named principal and an unnamed 'fully licensed staff', those answers queue behind Cioffi, and nothing in the current stack gives the firm searchable project memory - the site is static hand-coded HTML with no portal, no drawing-issue tooling and no file-transfer tool, so project documents live in email and local folders.
evidence: Deliverables are due diligence reports, feasibility studies, design peer reviews and design documents - each a reusable document asset - https://stoneridgeeng.com/due-diligence.html

About page names Robert Cioffi only and refers to a 'fully licensed staff' without roles, so there is no visible second point of technical authority (inference: answers concentrate on him) - https://stoneridgeeng.com/about.html
No client portal, file-transfer or drawing-issue tooling visible; document exchange happens off-site, inferred to be email - https://stoneridgeeng.com/index.html

Service scope spans mechanical, electrical, plumbing and fire protection plus emergency/standby power and building/facility surveys, so the reference corpus is broad across systems and building types - https://stoneridgeeng.com/mep-engineering.html

ACEC Research Institute 2025: AI use in design and project delivery is only 36% of firms versus 81% in marketing and sales - the delivery-side knowledge work is where the adoption gap sits (self-reported survey) - https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/

Licensed-PE accountability: AI output must be reviewed and sealed by the responsible licensee, so any drafting agent has to be a draft-only tool - constraint recorded in the industry brief (NCEES/state board guidance) - https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/
opportunities.agent_design: Single-tenant retrieval index (on-prem or dedicated cloud instance, no shared consumer chat) built over the firm's own material: past due diligence reports, feasibility studies, peer-review letters, RFI responses, specifications, standard details and the firm's code-basis notes. Three modes. (1) Staff Q&A: ask in plain English, get an answer with a citation to the exact source document and page, plus 'not found' rather than a guess. (2) Repeat-client mode: the same index filtered to one client's documents, so a broker or owner's question about their own building can be answered (or a reply drafted for Cioffi to send). (3) Draft assembly: given a new building type and scope, assemble a due-diligence or feasibility report skeleton from the closest prior reports, with every assumption, code reference and figure marked as unverified draft. Human approval: Cioffi reviews every engineering conclusion, and the agent is barred from issuing, sealing or transmitting anything; answers are logged so a wrong retrieval is traceable. Client NDA scoping means one client's documents are never retrievable from another's session.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Consumer chat tools require uploading client PDFs to a third party, offer no per-client access control, no citations back to a page, and no way to keep a licensed firm's confidential reports inside its own boundary. The work is ingestion and OCR of mixed PDFs and scanned reports, a permissioned index, an evaluation set to prove answer accuracy, and a review gate - none of which a subscription provides, and all of which the firm's NDAs require.

impact_estimate.range: 1-4 hours a week of principal and staff time currently spent hunting prior reports and re-assembling boilerplate report sections, ~$50-$200/week at the NJ civil engineer median ($50.32/hr). Conservative because question volume is unmeasured and the first months go partly into indexing.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Transfers the 40% completion-time reduction measured on 20-30 minute professional writing tasks (preregistered experiment, 453 professionals, Science 2023) to report assembly only; it does not assume any reduction in engineering review time, which stays with the PE. Assumes the firm keeps digital copies of past reports back far enough to be useful - unverified, no portal or document system is visible.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: index 12-24 months of one client's or one building type's reports and standard details; a 20-question evaluation set with Cioffi scoring answer correctness and citation accuracy; measure time-to-answer against manual searching; one assembled report skeleton reviewed line by line; a written data-handling note the firm can show a client or their counsel.

lead_score.rationale: Pain: the front door fails on live inspection - contact form with no working submit, no tel: link, dead mobile menu, unclaimed Google profile, zero structured data - but there are no reviews, no analytics, no published revenue, and the intake and knowledge pains are inference from the site rather than statements by the firm, so not full marks. Fit: G, A and C map directly to observed gaps, with the licensed-PE review gate as a designed-in human approval point rather than an obstacle. Ability to pay: MEP/FP design and due diligence are high-ticket, but this is a principal-led firm of roughly 3-10 people (The Org lists 5 people; the 11-50 band looks like a directory default), with revenue, pipeline and headcount unconfirmed and one owner holding the chequebook. Ease: the G work is days not months and free to start with a Google claim, though the single unlisted contact address and no published email add friction to getting the engagement itself. Strategic: the pattern repeats across the North Brunswick/Route 1 corridor's many small MEP, structural and civil consultancies - unclaimed listings, dead 2010s static sites, document-heavy proposal work - so the offer is productisable. Capability E was deliberately not used: there is no avenues.json in this folder, and the business is a design office in a single leased suite with no owned inventory, fleet, production floor or equipment to instrument - its physical work happens in client buildings, so cameras or sensors would mean monitoring someone else's premises with no process of Stone Ridge's own to improve. If the owner wants E explored for this account it needs a verified avenue first.

best_evidence_signal: The contact form cannot submit at all - it posts to javascript:void(0) and its jQuery is blocked as mixed content, so a web-preferring prospect gets nothing - https://stoneridgeeng.com/contact.html
suggested_channel: phone - no email address is published on the site or the Google profile, and the only working intake is (732) 658-6302; a walk-in at the Suite 4 Livingston Ave office is the fallback
